title: Introducing ChatGPT agent
claim: Research, browser, terminal and connectors coordinated for multi-step tasks.
limitations: Launch post now explicitly marked outdated; prior-art evidence, not current availability or unified Voice compatibility.

title: ChatGPT Agent System Card — security controls
claim: Layered prompt-injection mitigations, user confirmations and Watch Mode are documented.
limitations: Security-control search excerpts inspected; fetched page is a partial system-card extract. Historical design and vendor evaluation, not independent proof or complete present-day policy.

title: ChatGPT agent — current help overview
claim: Overview says ChatGPT agent is no longer available and points to ChatGPT Work; subsequent legacy sections still describe agent behavior.
limitations: Mixed current overview and legacy body; do not present historical agent instructions as guaranteed current availability.

title: Talk naturally with Gemini Live
claim: Natural interruption-capable voice and selected Connected Apps actions are documented, including Calendar, Tasks and Keep.
limitations: Gradual rollout and account/platform restrictions; exact Vietnamese feature performance not tested.

title: Architecting Security for Agentic Capabilities in Chrome
claim: Separate User Alignment Critic, origin isolation/gating, consequential-action confirmations and prompt-injection checks.
limitations: Vendor architecture disclosure; no independent immunity guarantee. Exact rollout may differ from design article.

title: Gemini Computer Use
claim: Models propose browser/mobile/desktop UI actions; client executes them and handles allow/confirmation/blocked safety decisions.
limitations: Developer building block, not a turnkey consumer assistant; version-specific feature/model availability untested.

title: Voice features in Microsoft Copilot FAQ
claim: Windows hands-free activation is opt-in; FAQ says not all text features work in voice and voice chats with Copilot agents are not currently supported.
limitations: Rollout, subscription and region vary; do not conflate Voice, Vision and Actions into one universally supported flow.

title: Supported languages for Microsoft Copilot
claim: Vietnamese is explicitly listed among Copilot Voice languages for personal Microsoft accounts.
limitations: Listed support does not establish dialect/slot accuracy or feature parity in NORA's test tasks.

title: Considerations for Safe Agentic Browsing
claim: Edge documents relevance checks, Task Tracker in testing, sensitive-site prompts and restrictions on agent actions.
limitations: Preview-era design; Task Tracker described as testing, not guaranteed deployed behavior or measured NORA comparison.

title: Browse with Copilot
claim: Local browser actions, visible progress/takeover, site access controls and requests for attention on sensitive actions.
limitations: Local browser execution does not mean local model inference. Experimental, may err or follow malicious hidden instructions.

title: Introducing Alexa+
claim: Natural voice, smart home, booking/shopping and orchestration through groups called experts.
limitations: Announcements and updated marketing mix available/future capabilities; not independent performance proof or verified Vietnamese support.

title: Use Apple Intelligence in Shortcuts
claim: Shortcuts can combine app actions with on-device, Private Cloud Compute or ChatGPT model outputs.
limitations: Apple ecosystem/device restrictions; Apple Intelligence Vietnamese support must not be equated with all Siri AI beta features.

title: Apple Intelligence availability and requirements
claim: Apple Intelligence lists Vietnamese and details device/OS/platform/language feature availability.
limitations: Individual features differ. Initial Siri AI beta list in companion docs excludes Vietnamese; no broad all-feature Vietnamese claim.

title: Set up a fully local voice assistant — Home Assistant
claim: Local STT–intent–TTS with Speech-to-Phrase/Whisper and Piper; voice request has no inherent user identity and requires configured acts-as-user mapping.
limitations: Home automation focus; language quality and open-ended task support differ; published speed examples are not NORA benchmarks.

title: Best practices with Assist
claim: Entity exposure is opt-in; least exposure improves performance and reduces LLM context cost.
limitations: Entity scope is not a general desktop filesystem sandbox or proof of speaker identity.

title: OpenClaw tool and agent permissions
claim: Per-agent sandbox/tool profiles and filesystem/session controls are documented; cross-agent visibility needs separate settings.
limitations: Configuration-specific; profile names alone do not guarantee isolation, and no Windows resource/voice benchmark was run.

title: OpenClaw sandboxing
claim: Tool execution may use a sandbox backend; sandboxing is off by default, Gateway remains on host, tool deny policy still applies.
limitations: Project explicitly says not a perfect boundary; index/version snapshot, not an audited NORA deployment.

title: OpenClaw prompt injection guidance
claim: Hard controls, tool policies, approvals, sandboxing and channel allowlists remain necessary despite model robustness.
limitations: Referenced attack-rate numbers were not independently verified and are not reused as comparative evidence.

title: Mitigating Prompt Injection in Comet
claim: Comet describes real-time classifiers, model guardrails, confirmations and transparent security notifications.
limitations: Vendor disclosure and marketing; no claim all attacks are prevented or no latency overhead exists.

title: BrowseSafe — Perplexity
claim: Defense-in-depth, untrusted-content boundaries, hybrid classification and evaluation benchmark are described.
limitations: Partial article inspected; vendor benchmark distribution is not a Vietnamese/Zalo task benchmark or an immunity proof.

title: Managing Comet Assistant permissions
claim: Enterprise admins can control browser actions/domain scope and consent behavior.
limitations: Enterprise options and claims apply to relevant account/configuration; certifications not independently audited in this review.

title: Work with Browsers and Apps — Perplexity
claim: Voice request entry is available on Windows/Mac; page distinguishes Mac installed-app control from connectors.
limitations: The inspected page says installed-app control is Mac-only. Do not infer Windows app control or all Comet actions from voice entry alone.

title: ChatGPT Voice FAQ
claim: Voice is conversational; current Live option supports web search/memory but initially not connected apps/plugins.
limitations: Voice options vary by plan/region/app version. Separate agent capability does not establish feature parity within Voice.

title: CaMeL — Defeating Prompt Injections by Design
claim: CaMeL extracts trusted control/data flow and tracks capabilities including provenance/allowed readers to enforce tool data-flow policy.
limitations: Paper's guarantee applies to stated assumptions/interpreter and evaluated scope, not arbitrary GUIs or NORA. Partial full-text sections inspected.

title: The Task Shield
claim: Task Shield checks whether instructions and tool calls contribute to user goals and reports utility/security results on AgentDojo.
limitations: Abstract/record and search excerpts inspected, not full experiments reproduced; results are model/benchmark-specific.

title: RTBAS — Defending LLM Agents Against Prompt Injection and Privacy Leakage
claim: Information-flow-style integrity/confidentiality checks allow safe tool calls automatically and ask users when safeguards cannot be ensured.
limitations: Full-text introduction/method excerpts inspected, experiments not reproduced; abstract's all-targeted-attacks result is finite and scope-specific.

title: Multilingual-BFCL / Teaching Small Models When Not to Call Functions
published_on_or_unknown: exact artifact release date unknown; linked paper published 2026-07-10
claim: Authors describe BFCL-VN/TH, 3,641 samples per language in the paper's BFCL v3 single-turn scope, tool-use/refusal/hallucination metrics, and explicit exclusion of multi-turn/long-context from reported experiments.
limitations: Card contains additional BFCL v4-style files outside reported scope. Data, evaluator and training were not downloaded or reproduced. No NORA hardware inference from small-model size. Live card may change.

title: Vietnamese Function Calling Benchmark — phamhai
claim: Card describes 2,899 single-turn Vietnamese function-calling samples, 159 functions and domain coverage including banking, insurance, travel, shopping and work; name and exact-argument metrics.
limitations: Author-reported sizes/results; dataset not downloaded, provenance/license not audited, no audio or stateful attack-recovery protocol documented in inspected card. Historical score revisions exist, so no model-score comparison imported into NORA.

title: V-Bench — Dataset and Submission/Scoring Specification
claim: Original CAIR/VinUniversity site documents Agentic function-call JSONL scoring with schema/required/enum constraints; current public scoring marks Safety inactive.
limitations: Live documentation, not independently evaluated; version label and displayed date differ by a day. Did not download public test or access professional/private test, so do not infer their complete scope or reuse rights.

title: V-Bench — Vietnamese LLM Benchmark
claim: Website explicitly includes agentic capability alongside Vietnamese knowledge, culture and safety categories.
limitations: Headline counts and leaderboard are author-operated and were not independently validated or used for NORA superiority claims. Safety category must not be conflated with indirect-injection recovery.

title: Teaching Small Models When Not to Call Functions: Structured Reasoning for Tool Refusal in Low-Resource Languages
claim: SIGIR research record confirms Vietnamese/Thai tool refusal work using lightweight structured reasoning, joint capability/refusal evaluation, and malformed-call intent metric concerns.
limitations: Abstract/record inspected; no experiment reproduced and no full training package downloaded. Reported improvements are specific to authors' models and benchmark and are not NORA results.
